evals.prompt: Can you review src/components/AccountSummaryCard.tsx before I open the PR? It uses hearth-react — I want to make sure I haven't missed anything obvious around styling, tokens, or accessibility.
evals.expected_output: A tiered list of findings: Card's `shadow` prop doesn't exist (Tier 1 — hallucinated prop); raw `style={{ padding: '16px' }}` bypasses tokens (Tier 2); `marginRight` on a sibling instead of `gap` on the Flex parent (Tier 2); `<Heading>` missing `as` (Tier 1 — accessibility); standalone icon with no `title`/`titleId` (Tier 1 — accessibility); CSS variable string used in JS instead of a browser token (Tier 2); `marginLeft="auto"` instead of `justifyContent` on the wrapper (Tier 2).
expectations: Flags Card's `shadow` prop as not existing on the component, verified against docs rather than assumed
Flags the raw px `style={{ padding: '16px' }}` as bypassing the token system
Flags `marginRight` used for spacing between siblings instead of `gap` on the parent Flex
Flags `<Heading>` missing the `as` prop as an accessibility gap
Flags the CSS variable string in the `style` prop as should be a browser token instead
Flags `marginLeft="auto"` as a margin hack that should be `justifyContent` on the Flex wrapper
Findings are grouped into tiers rather than presented as a flat list
Does not report every prop usage as an error — correct usage (Card/CardContent, Flex, BodyText, onClick) is left unflagged

evals.prompt: Please review src/components/DeleteConfirmModal.tsx against our Hearth React guidelines before merge — want to make sure I'm not missing anything.
evals.expected_output: Findings covering: the hand-rolled overlay `<div>` should use Modal's own compound sub-components instead of custom markup; the responsive `padding={{ tablet: '300' }}` object is missing the required `mobile` key so nothing applies at mobile size; the `Button` wrapped in a raw `<a>` without `asChild` produces invalid HTML (button inside anchor).
expectations: Flags the hand-rolled `<div>` overlay as compound-component misuse — should use Modal's own sub-components instead of custom markup, even though Modal is imported
Flags the responsive padding object `{ tablet: '300' }` as missing the required `mobile` breakpoint
Flags the `Button` wrapped in a raw `<a>` without `asChild` as invalid HTML nesting
Findings are grouped into tiers rather than presented as a flat list

evals.prompt: Can you review src/components/SavingsDisclaimer.tsx? It uses hearth-react and I want to check it follows the design system before I open the PR.
evals.expected_output: Tiered findings covering: `Link asChild` wrapping an `<a>` when `Link` already renders an `a`; the hand-rolled visually hidden "(opens in new tab)" text, which `Link` already handles with its open-in-new-tab icon for `target="_blank"`; `Link` used inside body text where the docs name `InlineLink` as the alternative; `style={{ width: '100%' }}` on `Button` instead of the documented column `Flex` full-width pattern; `style={{ flex: 1 }}` on `Box` instead of the `flex` style prop.
expectations: Flags `<Link asChild><a>` as unnecessary because `Link` already renders an `a` element
Flags the visually hidden "(opens in new tab)" span as duplicating `Link`'s built-in open-in-new-tab icon, rather than suggesting a different way to hide the text
Suggests `InlineLink` for the link inside the `BodyText` paragraph, citing the Link docs' alternatives
Flags `style={{ width: '100%' }}` on `Button` and recommends the documented column `Flex` full-width pattern
Flags `style={{ flex: 1 }}` on `Box` as an inline style where the `flex` style prop exists
Findings are grouped into tiers rather than presented as a flat list
